{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My bandmate had a chance to audition for a famous producer but couldn't afford the flight. I sold my vintage guitar—the one my late brother gave me—to buy her ticket. She got signed. She still thinks I won that money gambling. I'll let her keep believing that.

CANDIDATE A:
My elderly neighbor's grandson needed a kidney transplant. I was a match, so I donated anonymously through the hospital's program. The family believes a stranger saved him. I watch him play in the yard and have never said a word.

CANDIDATE B:
My bandmate couldn't afford the flight to audition for that same famous producer, so I lent her the money and told her straight that it came from me. She paid me back once she got signed. We still laugh about the loan that launched her career.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:23"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a selfless act of sacrifice for someone else's benefit, with the giver remaining anonymous and allowing the recipient to believe in a different narrative."}
